newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's bond yields end lower, trading slow.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's bond yields end lower, trading slow.

text.p: Benchmark three-year bond yields ended lower on Thursday on active buying by securities firms, but trading was slow with investment trust firms staying on the sidelines, dealers said.
Three-month CD yields closed lower on the back of improved cash liquidity.
The central bank's announcement of August M2 money supply figures had little impact on the money market, they said.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.15 pct vs Wednesday's 12.16
* 3-mth CDs end at 13.76 pct vs Wednesday's 14.00
* Overnight call average at 13.00 pct vs Wednesday's 14.50
Corporate bond yields hit an intra-day low of 12.10 percent in the morning but closed the day at 12.15 percent due to profit-taking late in the session, dealers said.
The overnight call rate fell to an average of 13.00 percent from Wednesday's 14.50 percent on the back of the flush cash liquidity, they said.

The Bank of Korea's announcement of August M2 money supply figures had little impact on the money market. The bank announced August M2 money supply rose 17.4 percent year-on-year, against a 14.7 percent growth a year earlier.
